limits: Only ridge and one resource; forty splits per seed.
Seeds are fresh for this protocol but not for the programme as a whole.
Retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim.

the_headline_reproduces_under_fresh_seed.reading: three seeds that had never been used for this protocol each land inside [0.0947, 0.1409], and each one's own interval excludes zero. The point estimates span 0.113 to 0.127 around a reference of 0.118.

the_interval_is_not_optimistic.reading: the seed-to-seed spread is about a sixth of the interval width. So the interval I reported is conservative with respect to reseeding, not narrow. That is the opposite of the worry that motivated this round.

why_this_contrasts_with_R183.R183: a stratum estimate flipped significance between seeds
why_this_contrasts_with_R183.here: the headline does not move outside its interval under three fresh seeds
why_this_contrasts_with_R183.the difference: the headline pools forty splits with roughly four thousand evaluation rows per split, so its standard error is small. R183's stratum was a fraction of that, with an estimate sitting near the boundary of zero. The same machinery behaves correctly in both cases: it is well behaved when the quantity is well powered and unstable when it is not.
why_this_contrasts_with_R183.so: R183 was not evidence that my intervals are too narrow; it was evidence that a small quantity near zero will flip

what_this_adds_to_the_claim.before: the headline magnitude had been recomputed once at a tuned penalty (R163)
what_this_adds_to_the_claim.now: it has been reproduced under three independent reseedings of the whole split protocol, all inside the reported interval
what_this_adds_to_the_claim.status: the most reproduced number in the programme
what_this_adds_to_the_claim.what_it_does_not_add: it does not touch the cross-dataset question, which remains an external dependency (C140)
